Oakwood Bottoms & Turkey Bayou Campground
A favorite with waterfowl hunters, Oakwood Bottoms offers so much more from excellent bird watching to fishing opportunities and primitive camping at Turkey Bayou Campground. Picnic with your family or youth group at Oakwood Bottoms picnic site and take a short walk into the bottoms on the wooden boardwalk trail that loops back to the picnic area. The site also has a large picnic shelter next to a large pond, where you can enjoy watching ducks and other birds visit the pond in search of food.
Big Muddy Boat Launch also offers one of the few locations to launch your boat or kayak onto the Big Muddy River.
Active Alerts
Failing Culvert on Oakwood Bottoms Road FSR # 786
General Information
Turkey Bayou Campground​
Located in Oakwood Bottoms, Turkey Bayou Campground is a great location outdoor activities including waterfowl hunting, deer hunting, trapping, fishing, nature watching and bird watching. The campground is next to a 20-acre lake on the Big Muddy River with close proximity to the Big Muddy boat launch and the Oakwood Bottoms Greentree Reservoir. There is no charge for camping at Turkey Bayou, but there is a 14-day maximum stay. The campground does not have water. The site frequently floods during heavy rain periods.
Our partner, Friends of Turkey Bayou maintain Turkey Bayou Campground.
Fishing Regulations:
LgSmallmouth bass -16” min. Daily limit=3
Pure Muskellunge – 48” minimum length
White/Black or Hybrid Crappie – 9: min. Daily limit=25
For site specific regulations or to obtain a fishing license go to Illinois fishing regulations.
Watercraft Motor Restriction on Turkey Bayou Lake is electric only.

Directions
To Oakwood Bottoms Picnic Area:
From Murphysboro: Take Highway 149 west 7 miles to Highway 3; then south 5.5 miles on Hwy 3 to Oakwood Bottoms Road. Turn east (left) onto Oakwood Bottoms Rd. and continue 1 mile to Oakwood Bottoms.
From Jonesboro: Take Highway 146 west 8 miles to Highway 3, then north 8 miles on Hwy 3 to John Spur Road. Turn east (right) onto Oakwood Bottoms and continue 1 mile to Oakwood Bottoms.
To Turkey Bayou Campground:
From Murphysboro: Take Highway 149 west 7 miles to Highway 3; then south 5.5 miles on Hwy 3 to Oakwood Bottoms Road. Turn east (left) onto Oakwood Bottoms Rd. and continue 4 miles to the campground.
From Jonesboro: Take Highway 146 west 8 miles to Highway 3, then north 8 miles on Hwy 3 to Oakwood Bottoms Road. Turn east (right) onto Oakwood Bottoms Rd. and continue 4 miles to the campground.
To Big Muddy Boat Launch:
From Murphysboro: Take Highway 149 west 7 miles to Highway 3; then south 5.5 miles on Hwy 3 to Oakwood Bottoms Road. Turn east (left) onto Oakwood Bottoms Rd. and go 3.5 miles, boat launch is straight ahead at curve.
From Jonesboro: Take Highway 146 west 8 miles to Highway 3, then north 8 miles on Hwy 3 to Oakwood Bottoms Road. Turn east (right) onto Oakwood Bottoms Rd. and go 3.5 miles, boat launch is straight ahead at curve.

Habitat: This area is rolling with steep hills and deep hollows, covered with mature timber of oak-hickory type. The entire area is well supplied with water from springs interspersed throughout the area. Agricultural leases maintain open areas to provide habitat diversity.
Active habitat management will be occurring throughout the year on the site, including prescribed burning.

Welcome to North Point Marina - the largest marina on the Great Lakes - a world-class facility offering public access to Lake Michigan from a quiet, serene and safe setting on the breathtakingly beautiful Illinois lakeshore.
North Point Marina sports a protected floating dock system of 1,500 slips from 30 to 60 feet, ideally located at the midpoint between Chicago and Milwaukee.
North Point Marina is adjacent to Illinois Beach State Park, one of the nation'​s most beautiful state parks, preserving the last remaining shore in the state with natural coastal dunes and wetlands, high quality coastal fauna, and outstanding recreation.

Site Characteristics
Huntable acres: 1351
Habitat: Copperhead Hollow has steep hills and deep hollows, covered with oak-hickory forest. Agricultural leases provide and maintain open areas to increase habitat diversity. There are also small brushy areas interspersed across the site.
Active habitat management will occur throughout the year on the site, including prescribed burning.
Site Specific Regulations
Statewide and associated species regulations apply at the site unless noted hereafter.
Site requires use of windshield card, displayed on the vehicle dashboard, to report hunting effort and harvest by 15 February.
No ATV’s are allowed on site. Use of bicycles and low speed electric bicycles are NOT authorized except on roadways designated for vehicular use.
No target or trap shooting is allowed.
No unauthorized person may use or occupy this area during any hunting season when authorized hunting is in progress.
Parking is only allowed in the parking lots.
Tracking deer with dogs is prohibited during hours when deer hunting is being conducted on site.

Hunters with a valid, unfilled firearm deer permit for the hunt area may take coyotes during legal hours of the firearm deer season. Otherwise, the use of shotgun slugs to take furbearing mammals is prohibited on state sites.
.224 caliber or smaller centerfire is allowed from the close of deer season until the end of the statewide fox season.
Coyote and striped skunk season coincides with the statewide fox season.
Trapping

Permits are issued via a public drawing held the Wednesday after the opening of the central waterfowl season at the Mississippi River SFWA site office.
All persons entering the drawing must have a current trapping license and habitat stamp.
Site specific regulations will be provided to permit holders.
